# Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

Implementation task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC3).

## Goal

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

## Minimal implementation

- In `GymFormationScene`, add an injectable RNG (`protected rng: () => number = Math.random` plus a `setRng()`/config seam) used for mineral drops.
- Add a single `_spawnMineralKillDrops(entity)` path that calls `resolveMineralKillDrops(...)` and registers the returned minerals in the gym's mineral field.
- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`, `explodeRandom`, RNG seam, mineral field.

# Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions)

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 6). **Depends on:** child #1 (player tick).

## Summary

`PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` advances the boss inside `tick`, before collisions; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` and *then* advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick(dt)` never advances the boss and bullet timing/ordering differs. `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies()` makes P7 teleport avoid the boss; `GymBoss` does not. `PlayScene._spawnMinions` spawns phase minions; the gym has no equivalent. Move boss advancement onto the shared tick path (via a hook) and align teleport avoidance and minion spawning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — Boss advancement is a shared hook called from `tick`, so a single `tick(dt)` advances the boss in both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` with the same ordering relative to collisions. Verified by a cross-scene test asserting boss bullets appear after the same `tick`.
- [ ] **AC2** — P7 teleport avoids the boss in `GymBoss` as in the game (shared `getAdditionalTeleportBodies` behaviour).
- [ ] **AC3** — Phase-minion spawning matches the game (or is an explicitly documented, producer-approved constrained-feature difference). If mirrored, `GymBoss` uses the shared `planMinionSpawns`.
- [ ] **AC4** — No observable game change; all `PlayScene` boss tests and `GymBoss` tests pass.
- [ ] **AC5** — All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5 and the `GymBoss` docstring.
- [ ] **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_updateBoss` delegates.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — remove `update` override; implement hooks.

# Intake Brief — More enemy variety in the first 3-4 waves

**Headline:** Make the campaign's first four waves (Level 1 waves 1–2 and Level 2 waves 1–2) build with the `dynamic` generation mode so each run opens on a varied mix of existing enemy archetypes instead of repeated Scouts — while preserving the no-enemy-fire onboarding boundary and the retuned-campaign difficulty ramp.

## Seed description

There is a lot of repition in the first few waves, introduce more enemy variety.

## Problem statement

The shipped campaign opens with the same enemy for three waves in a row: L1W1 `scout x6`, L1W2 `scout x8`, L2W1 `scout x8`, then L2W2 `diver x8`. Levels 1–3 are generation mode `fixed`, so they reuse the hand-authored static `LEVELS` waves verbatim and never vary between runs. The opening is therefore repetitive and under-exposes the enemy roster.

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, I want the opening waves to feature different enemy types rather than the same Scouts, so the first minutes feel varied and teach more of the roster.
- **As a player**, I want the opening waves to vary between runs, so repeat playthroughs feel fresh.
- **As a designer**, I want the added variety to preserve the onboarding difficulty ramp and the no-enemy-fire boundary (GDD §2.4/§3.2), so early play stays approachable and consistent with the rest of the campaign.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Dynamic, non-firing opening.** The first four campaign waves (L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2) have `generation: dynamic` and remain non-firing (`shootEnabled === false`). *Verification:* assert `generation` and `shootEnabled` on `buildSequencedLevels()` output; the fire boundary for levels 1–3 is unchanged.
- **AC2 — Real variety.** Across the four waves at the default seed, at least three distinct existing enemy archetypes appear, and no two of the four waves share an identical composition. *Verification:* unit test on the built campaign.
- **AC3 — Per-run variation with reproducibility.** The four dynamic waves differ across at least two distinct run seeds, while each seed reproduces its campaign exactly (dynamic is a pure function of curve, pool and seed; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent). *Verification:* build with ≥2 seeds and assert variation plus same-seed equality.
- **AC4 — No regression of the retuned campaign.** The first four waves are non-degenerate: no asteroid-only wave and no 1-count wave in levels 1–3; the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins still pass (no-degeneracy, non-decreasing targets within and across levels, strictly rising aggregated difficulty, fire boundary held). *Verification:* existing/updated regression suite.
- **AC5 — Defaults and seed agree.** `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` both mark L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic` with matching retuned targets, and every other wave's mode/target is unchanged. *Verification:* config-store and CSV seed tests.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** New or updated unit/integration tests cover mode dispatch, seed variation and reproducibility, the non-degeneracy guarantee and the difficulty ramp; the full project test suite passes.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the GDD (§3.2 Level 1 description and the default-campaign note) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Constraints

- **Existing archetypes only** (producer decision 1→2a): re-mix `scout`, `diver`, `tank`, `swarm`, `phaser` (and the roaming `asteroid`); do **not** add or invent new enemy archetypes.
- **Dynamic and non-firing** (producer decision 3b): the four waves regenerate per run from their curve and seed, but levels 1–3 must not fire (GDD §2.4/§3.2 boundary).
- **Must not regress AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K**: no asteroid-only and no 1-count wave in levels 1–3; targets non-decreasing; aggregated difficulty strictly rising; fire boundary held.
- **Determinism contract** (AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT): `curve`/`fixed` waves are seed-independent; `dynamic` waves are a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed).
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): the campaign builder is shared core; any gym that exercises it must stay consistent.
- UK English in all code comments, tests and documentation.

## Existing state

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` marks levels 1–3 `fixed`, levels 4–5 `curve`, and L5W2 `dynamic`.
- `src/core/configStore.ts`: `DEFAULT_FIXED_LEVELS = {1,2,3}`, `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES = {5:{2:'dynamic'}}`, `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES = {4:[16,24,28], 5:[45,62]}`. `defaultDifficultyCurves()` emits each wave's mode as `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES[level]?.[wave] ?? (fixed ? 'fixed' : 'curve')`, so per-wave override of a `fixed` level is already supported with no new mechanism.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` dispatches per wave on `generation`. A `dynamic` wave applies a seed-derived ±`DYNAMIC_TARGET_JITTER` (20) shift to its target before re-sequencing; `fixed` reuses the static `LEVELS` wave verbatim.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`: `defaultCandidatePool()` is every archetype except `harvester`, with `count` as the only adjustable field; `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE = 10`; multi-group composition is on by default.
- Regression pin: `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` → describe "Retuned default campaign (AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K)".

### Feasibility finding (evidence)

Making the four waves `dynamic` with the **current** targets (3.01, 6.01, 7.66, 9.3) and the default pool reintroduces the exact degeneracy AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K removed. With the ±20 dynamic jitter the sequencer emits `asteroid x1` (or another 1-count group) for most seeds, and occasionally wildly inconsistent waves (`phaser x12`, `swarm x45`). Non-firing difficulty is nearly flat in enemy count — `scout x1 = 5.34` … `x6 = 5.89`, `asteroid x1 = 8.62`, `diver x1 = 11.55`, `swarm x1 = 12.76`, `tank x1 = 15.10`, `phaser x1 = 18.28` — so the default pool has no low-difficulty band that yields varied, non-degenerate waves. The early `curve` targets are also artificially low (roughly half the measured level score), which compounds this. The mode dispatch itself needs no new mechanism.

## Desired change

- Mark L1W1, L1W2, L2W1 and L2W2 as `dynamic` in both `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and the seed CSV (add them to `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES`); leave the rest of levels 1–3 `fixed`.
- Resolve the degeneracy so the four dynamic waves are varied and non-degenerate at every seed — the mechanism is a **plan-stage decision** (see Open decision).
- Retune the four waves' targets so the opening ramp stays smooth and aggregated difficulty still rises from level 1 upward.
- Update the GDD (Level 1 "Scout V-formations" wording and the default-campaign note), README/design docs and code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — L1W1..L2W2 → `dynamic`; retuned targets.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_MODE_OVERRIDES` (add the four waves) and retuned early targets in `defaultDifficultyCurves()`.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — likely seam for a curated early-wave candidate pool and/or minimum-count floor (mechanism TBD at plan).
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — candidate-pool/tolerance/jitter tuning if the chosen mechanism requires it.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — update/extend the regression pins and add variety/determinism assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.2, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — document the dynamic opening and the curation.

## Open decision (resolve at planning)

How to make low-difficulty dynamic waves varied and non-degenerate **without new archetypes**. Recommended approach: give the opening waves a **curated early-game candidate pool** (e.g. `scout`/`diver`/`swarm`/`tank`, excluding `asteroid`/`boss`/`phaser`) with a **minimum-count floor** (count ≥ ~4) and retune their targets into a narrow ascending band, so the sequencer selects a different light archetype per wave and the seed jitter varies the mix across runs while the no-degeneracy regression still passes. Alternatives: reduce/parameterise `DYNAMIC_TARGET_JITTER`; tighten the sequencer tolerance; or compose the opening waves from multiple groups. Whichever is chosen must satisfy AC1–AC5.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed) — established the no-degeneracy/ramp regression this change must preserve.
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: `curve`, `fixed` and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed) — the mode dispatch and the determinism contract.
- **AH-0MUJSUTLA006Q8E1** — Enable sequenced wave generation by default with a mixed-mode initial campaign (completed) — the shipped mixed-mode campaign.
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** — Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed) — asteroids are a roaming hazard, not a wave group.
- **AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63** / **AH-0MUITRZZE000OYQE** — difficulty-curve / runtime auto-sequencer programme (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — degeneracy recurrence (high, evidenced):** dynamic + low targets yields asteroid-only/1-count waves. *Mitigation:* AC4 regression plus the Open-decision mechanism.
- **Risk — difficulty-ramp inversion:** raising early targets to avoid degeneracy can push levels 1–2 towards level 4. *Mitigation:* keep the four targets in an ascending band below L4W1 (16) and assert rising aggregated difficulty (AC4).
- **Risk — seed jitter is erratic at low targets:** ±20 is large relative to a ~5–15 target band. *Mitigation:* narrow the band/curate the pool, or reduce/parameterise the jitter (plan decision).
- **Risk — scope creep:** adding new archetypes, reworking later levels, or changing global difficulty tuning is out of scope; record such ideas as linked work items.
- **Assumption (producer, 1a):** "first 3-4 waves" = the campaign's first four waves (L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2).
- **Assumption (producer, 2a):** re-mix existing archetypes only; no new archetypes.
- **Assumption (producer, 3b):** the four waves are `dynamic` (per-run variation) and non-firing.
- **Assumption (to confirm at plan):** the degeneracy mechanism is resolved per the Open decision; implementation may add a per-wave candidate-pool / count-floor seam.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q (round 1): "Scope — which waves are 'the first 3-4 waves'?" — Answer (producer): **"(a)"** = the first 3-4 waves of the whole campaign (L1W1, L1W2, L2W1, L2W2), including Level 1. Source: interactive reply, this session (work-item comment `AH-C0MUPJFJ0Z007UOA6`).
- Q (round 1): "Archetype source — re-mix existing enemies or add new archetypes?" — Answer (producer): **"(a)"** = re-mix the existing archetypes only (scout, diver, tank, swarm, phaser, asteroid). Source: comment `AH-C0MUPJFL95001OIUF`.
- Q (round 1): "Determinism and fire boundary — should early waves stay fixed and non-firing?" — Answer (producer): **"(b)"** = convert the early waves to dynamic so they vary per run but still do not fire. Source: comment `AH-C0MUPJFNXN004MC54`.
- Research (agent): the opening repetition is because levels 1–3 are `fixed`; the no-degeneracy and fire-boundary constraints come from AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K; dynamic + current low targets is degenerate (empirical finding above). Source: repo inspection, this session.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A** – Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed)
- **AH-0MUJRW0GV007JK6S** – Campaign roaming Harvester spawns (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: create, enemy, first, introduce, lot (+2 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: create, enemy, first, introduce, lot (+2 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: create, enemy, first, lot, there (+1 more)

---

## Plan (decomposed 2026-10-01)

**Plan summary.** Resolve the intake Open decision with a measured spike, then
implement the dynamic, varied, non-firing opening as a test-first vertical
slice, and document it. Existing archetypes only; levels 1–3 stay non-firing;
the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins must keep passing.

**Approval gate:** not required — effort Small and risk Medium do not trigger a
human plan-approval pause (`plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` returned
`request_approval: false`).

### Features (children, in dependency order)

1. **Spike: validate dynamic opening-wave sequencing mechanism** — AH-0MUQ523AJ0064PR3
   *(task, high, Small/Medium)*. Determine and record the concrete mechanism
   and parameters (curated early candidate pool, minimum-count floor,
   parameterised jitter, four retuned ascending targets) that make L1W1..L2W2
   varied and non-degenerate across a seed sweep. Deliverable: decision record +
   parameter set. No dependencies.
2. **Tests: dynamic opening variety, determinism and regression** —
   AH-0MUQ523A90028N9B *(task, high, Small/Low)*. Add failing-first tests for the
   parent AC1–AC6: dynamic + non-firing opening, ≥3 distinct archetypes / four
   distinct compositions at the default seed, seed variation with same-seed
   reproducibility, no-degeneracy across seeds, unchanged regression pins, and
   defaults/CSV agreement. Depends on (1).
3. **Implement dynamic, varied non-firing opening waves** —
   AH-0MUQ5262M009UFLU *(feature, high, Small/Medium)*. Apply the spike
   mechanism in the shared core; mark L1W1..L2W2 `dynamic` in
   `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `difficulty-curves.csv` with matching
   retuned targets; keep gym↔game parity; make the tests green; build + full
   suite pass. Depends on (1) and (2).
4. **Document the dynamic, varied opening** — AH-0MUQ52620006N3SE
   *(docs, medium, Small/Low)*. Update GDD §3.2 (Level 1 wording and the
   default-campaign note), `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
   §9.6 and code comments; remove stale Scout-only / levels 1–3 fully-fixed
   claims. Depends on (3).

### Dependency edges

- Tests (2) → Spike (1)
- Implement (3) → Spike (1), Tests (2)
- Document (4) → Implement (3)

### Vertical-slice phasing

Each phase is a vertical slice for the work it covers. The spike cuts through
design + measurement + decision; the test slice encodes the observable
acceptance contract across the campaign builder and config/CSV surfaces; the
implementation slice applies the mechanism end-to-end (shared core, defaults,
CSV seed, comments) and makes the acceptance tests green; the docs slice
propagates the shipped behaviour to the player- and designer-facing
documentation. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update
it if the spike's findings change its parameters or scope.

### Open decision resolution

The intake Open decision ("how to keep low-difficulty dynamic waves varied and
non-degenerate without new archetypes") is delegated to child (1). The
implemented mechanism is whatever the spike validates; the intake-recommended
curated early pool + minimum-count floor + retuned ascending band (likely with
a reduced/parameterised jitter) is the starting point, not a commitment.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-01 — Initial plan: 4 children created (spike, tests, implement,
  docs), 4 dependency edges wired, effort/risk estimated for every child.
  Parent intake Appendix reviewed; no new interview questions were required
  (all product decisions already answered in intake). Mechanism deferred to the
  spike child per the intake Open decision.

### Appendix addendum (plan round)

- No new clarifying questions were asked in the plan round: the intake Appendix
  already resolves the product decisions (scope = first four campaign waves;
  existing archetypes only; dynamic and non-firing). The one remaining
  decision — the non-degeneracy mechanism — is explicitly a plan-stage
  engineering decision per the intake brief and is delegated to the spike child
  (AH-0MUQ523AJ0064PR3), whose acceptance criteria require measured evidence.

# Intake Brief — Make P9 Magnet timed on pickup and permanent-stack on upgrade (AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L)

**Headline:** Bring the **P9 Magnet** into line with the **P10 Mineral Scoop** hybrid model — a **15 s, refresh-only** timed drop-attraction for field pickups and a **permanent stacking (cap 5)** attraction for the hold-full upgrade — implemented once in the shared `EffectsRegistry` so the game and every gym run identical behaviour.

## Problem statement

The P9 Magnet is currently **always** a permanent stack (cap 5): every pickup, whether a field drop or a hold-full reward, permanently increases the attraction radius. The P10 Mineral Scoop (AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ) introduced a hybrid model — timed on field pickup, permanent-stacking on upgrade — and the operator requested during that intake that P9 be brought into line for design consistency. Until this change the two attraction power-ups share a radius curve but not the same duration/stacking semantics, which is an inconsistency the player can feel and the docs must paper over.

## Users

- **Player** — wants a predictable, escalating reward loop: a temporary convenience from a field drop, and a permanent, stacking boon from a deliberate hold-full choice.
- **Developer** — wants the magnet's timed/permanent behaviour defined once in the shared `EffectsRegistry` and consumed by every scene, so the game and gyms cannot drift.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I collect a **P9 Magnet** field drop, nearby drops drift toward my ship for **15 s** so pickups are easier; re-collecting refreshes the timer to full.
- As a player, when I choose P9 as a **hold-full reward**, the drop attraction becomes a permanent part of my run, so I never lose the convenience.
- As a developer, the magnet's timed/permanent behaviour is modelled once in the shared registry and every scene consumes the same effective-stacks accessor, so the game and gyms run identical code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Field pickup is a timed, refreshing effect.** `applyCollect('P9')` (the field-drop path, no `permanent` flag) activates a **15 s** drop-attraction effect; re-collecting refreshes the timer to full and **does not** add permanent stacks. Verified by unit tests in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (activation, expiry after 15 s, refresh, no permanent stack).
- [ ] **Hold-full upgrade is a permanent stacking effect.** `applyCollect('P9', true)` (the `applyMineralChoiceReward` path) grants a **permanent** attraction that stacks up to **5** and never decays on `tick`. Verified by unit tests in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` / `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`.
- [ ] **One shared effective-stacks accessor drives attraction.** A `magnetEffectStacks()` accessor (mirroring the existing `scoopEffectStacks()`) returns the permanent stack count when any upgrade was chosen, otherwise **1** while the timed field pickup is active, otherwise **0**. `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` consumes it, so `PlayScene` and every gym pull drops with identical range semantics; the repo-wide duplicate-body/equivalence parity guard stays green.
- [ ] **Help copy and documentation reflect the hybrid model.** The `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` description, GDD §4.4 table/notes and README power-up list describe P9 as "15 s timed pickup / permanent stacking when chosen as a reward (cap 5)", matching the P10 wording style.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Parity rule (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once in `src/powerups/` and `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both the game and the gyms; no divergent copy. The duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs assertion must stay green. Only a *disabled* feature may differ.
- **Duration (operator decision, parent intake Q1/Q5):** field pickup is **15 s**, refresh-only.
- **Timed radius (documented assumption):** while only the timed effect is active, use the minimum active radius — the equivalent of **one magnet stack** (`magnetRadius(shipSize, 1)` = `1 × 20 × 1.5` = **30 px** at `SHIP_SIZE = 20`), mirroring the P10 decision. Permanent stacks (≥ 1) define the radius when present. (Non-blocking; see Open questions.)
- **Single radius curve:** `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` remains the one source of truth for both P9 and P10 (`mineralScoopRadius` delegates to it) — do not fork or change its signature/semantics.
- **Cap stays 5:** `P9_MAX_STACKS` remains the permanent-stack cap; the timed path never stacks.
- **No new activation key:** the magnet stays passive.
- **Existing-test ripple:** today many tests call `applyCollect('P9')` (no flag) expecting permanent stacks (`src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, scene and gym tests). These must be updated to the **permanent** path (`applyCollect('P9', true)`) wherever they intend the upgrade, and the timed path covered by new tests. This is expected work, not a regression.
- **CHANGELOG.md is excluded** (ship skill owns it). Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) already models the P10 hybrid: `_scoopStacks`, `P10_MAX_STACKS`, `P10_SCOOP_DURATION = 15`, `isScoopActive()`, `scoopEffectStacks()`, and a `MINERAL_SCOOP` case that branches on `permanent`. The P9 `MAGNET` case currently **ignores** `permanent` and always increments `_magnetStacks` (cap `P9_MAX_STACKS`).
- `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` returns `MAGNET_RADIUS_BASE_MULTIPLIER (1) × shipSize × (1 + MAGNET_RADIUS_PER_STACK (0.5) × stacks)`. `mineralScoopRadius` delegates to it.
- `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` calls `applyDropMagnet(..., getEffectsRegistry().magnetStacks(), dt)` — the permanent-stack count only.
- The hold-full reward path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`) calls `effectsRegistry.applyCollect(option.id, true)` for power-up options; the field-drop path (`CombatCoreScene._collectDrop`) calls `applyCollect(dropId)` with no flag.
- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) has description "Permanently pulls nearby drops toward the ship (stacks up to 5)." and no `duration`; P10 carries `duration: 15` + `maxStacks: 5`.
- `activeEffects()` surfaces P9 permanent stacks as an `xN` row when `_magnetStacks > 0`; timed P10 surfaces from `_timed` plus a stack row (never `x0`). HUD `formatValue` renders `Ns` for timed rows and `xN` for stack rows.
- Existing tests assuming field-pickup permanence include `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (`P9 Magnet (AC4)`), `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` (HUD AC2), and scene/gym/drop-layer/equivalence tests that collect P9.

## Desired change

Make P9 a hybrid exactly analogous to P10:

- **Registry:** add `P9_MAGNET_DURATION = 15`; branch the `MAGNET` case on `permanent` (permanent → +1 stack capped at 5; field pickup → timed `_timed` entry, refresh-only); add `isMagnetActive()` and `magnetEffectStacks()`; include the timed P9 row and permanent P9 stack row (never `x0`) in `activeEffects()`; reset both states in `reset()`.
- **Scene wiring:** `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` consumes `magnetEffectStacks()` instead of `magnetStacks()`.
- **Catalogue:** add `duration: 15` to `P9` and rewrite its description to the hybrid wording.
- **Docs:** update GDD §4.4 (P9 row + notes) and README power-up/effects descriptions; remove the "tracked separately" note where it refers to this now-delivered change.
- **Tests:** extend `effects.test.ts` (timed activation/expiry/refresh, permanent stacking/cap, `magnetEffectStacks()`, `activeEffects()` shape, `reset()`), migrate existing field-pickup-as-permanent assertions to the permanent path, and keep parity/HUD/scene tests green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `P9_MAGNET_DURATION`, hybrid `MAGNET` case, `isMagnetActive()`, `magnetEffectStacks()`, `activeEffects()`, `reset()`; doc-comment updates.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `P9` catalogue `duration: 15` + hybrid description.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_applyDropMagnet` uses `magnetEffectStacks()`.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — timed/permanent P9 unit tests (mirroring the P10 block).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts` — permanent-path coverage if applicable.
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — migrate P9 stack assertions to the permanent path; add a timed-row case.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — effective-stacks pull + parity guard.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — scene-level P9 semantics/parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 P9 row + notes.
- `README.md` — power-up / shared-effects descriptions.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the timed/permanent split maps cleanly onto the existing `applyCollect(id, permanent)` flag, exactly as it did for P10. *Mitigation:* registry unit tests for both paths before scene wiring.
- **Risk — behavioural change ripples through existing tests.** Many tests use `applyCollect('P9')` to mean "permanent stack". *Mitigation:* systematically migrate those assertions to `applyCollect('P9', true)` and add explicit timed-path tests; the full suite must be green before `in_review`.
- **Risk — HUD dual timed/stacked display.** P9 changes type between pickups and upgrades; a stale `×0` would mislead. *Mitigation:* only surface stacks/remaining when active, mirroring P10's zero-suppression rule; add a HUD test.
- **Risk — parity drift.** If any scene computes its own stacks or radius, gyms diverge. *Mitigation:* one accessor (`magnetEffectStacks()`), shared `_applyDropMagnet`, and the duplicate-body/equivalence guard.
- **Risk — radius-curve coupling with P10.** `magnetRadius` is shared with the scoop; a careless change would alter P10. *Mitigation:* leave `magnetRadius` untouched and reuse it.
- **Assumption:** reusing the existing P9 pickup cue unchanged is acceptable; no new SFX required.
- **Assumption:** a timed P9 field pickup does **not** clear or cancel an existing permanent upgrade (and vice versa); the effective radius is driven by permanent stacks when present. Mirrors P10.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any generic "attractor target predicate" refactor or further P10 changes are out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ — Add a mineral scoop power-up** (completed): introduced the P10 hybrid timed-pickup/permanent-upgrade model and the `applyCollect(id, permanent)` pattern this item mirrors. `discovered-from` this item.

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: many (magnet, timed, permanent, pickup, upgrade, stack, cap, scoop, effects, gym, parity, tests, docs, …)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: many (magnet, timed, permanent, pickup, upgrade, stacking, cap, scoop, effects, parity, tests, docs, …)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No new interview round was required.** The design decision that determines this item's behaviour was already captured during the parent P10 intake: Q1 — "B when picked up in gameplay, A when added as an upgrade (create a work item to change the magnet to behave the same way)." Final accepted answer: field pickup = **timed**, hold-full upgrade = **permanent stacking**. Source: interactive reply recorded in AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ (`AH-C0MUQCYKT0000D52H`); the discovered-from work item is this item. The seed context supplied in the description therefore suffices to draft the brief, per the intake skill's "skip the interview when the seed context suffices" rule.

Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION for the producer (below) rather than blocking.

# Deterministic WAV build pipeline

## Goal

Create a build step that renders every game recipe to baked WAV assets under `public/audio/sfx/` via the ToneForge CLI, with recorded checksums, so the game bundle is self-contained and the generation step is reproducible in CI.

As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.

## Scope

- Add `scripts/build-audio.sh` that iterates the game recipe manifest, invokes `tf generate --recipe <slug> --seed <n> --output public/audio/sfx/<name>.wav`, and fails fast on any render error.
- Emit `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` (SHA-256 per asset) after a successful render.
- Add an `npm run build-audio` script and wire it into `npm run build` as a preceding step.
- Add a reproducibility check: re-rendering with the same seeds must reproduce identical checksums; drift fails the script.
- Add a CI step that runs `npm run build-audio` and fails if generated assets differ from the committed checksums.
- Handle pitch-jitter variants (explosions) by rendering a small fixed set of seeds and selecting among them at runtime.
- Thruster hum is out of scope for baking (handled by the runtime shim task).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run build-audio` renders all manifest recipes to `public/audio/sfx/` and exits non-zero on any failure.
- `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` records a SHA-256 for every rendered asset.
- Re-running `npm run build-audio` with unchanged seeds produces an identical `checksums.json`.
- `npm run build` invokes the audio build before the Vite bundle step.
- CI fails when a rendered asset's checksum does not match the committed manifest.
- The script's recipe manifest is a single source of truth consumed by both the build and the tests.
- No Node-only ToneForge dependency is bundled into the browser output (verified by build inspection).

## Dependencies

- Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (must exist before they can be rendered).

## Deliverables

- `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Recipe manifest file consumed by the script.
- `public/audio/sfx/` baked WAV assets plus `checksums.json`.
- `package.json` `build-audio` script and `build` wiring.
- CI job step invoking the build and verifying checksums.

- `../ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js` — `tf`/`toneforge` CLI entry point.

# Thruster hum Tone.js shim

## Goal

Implement the continuous, thrust-driven thruster hum as a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim, since baked WAV variants cannot reproduce a pitch/gain-continuous, thrust-coupled loop.

As the game's developer, I want the thruster hum to remain continuous and thrust-driven, so the tuning slider stays audible and the hum stays in lockstep with the flame animation.

## Scope

- Add a small Tone.js-based runtime shim that owns only the thruster hum; all other cues are baked assets (decision recorded on the parent epic).
- Preserve the existing `updateThrusterSound(level)` / `stopThrusterSound()` contract consumed by `Player.preUpdate`.
- Reproduce the documented character: triangle fundamental ~60 Hz + sine undertone ~35 Hz + band-pass filtered noise (700–1100 Hz) whoosh, gain ≤ 0.075.
- Mirror the flame growth/shrink timing (30 ms growth, ~4x decay) and avoid clicks on retrigger.
- Stop cleanly on release, respawn, player destroy and scene shutdown so no audio nodes leak.
- Degrade to a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- Add Tone.js as a pinned runtime dependency and verify it is the only new browser runtime dependency.

- The thruster hum is continuous while thrust is held and stops cleanly on release/respawn/destroy/scene shutdown.

- No clicks on retrigger; growth/decay match the documented flame timing.
- The shim is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- No audio nodes leak after repeated thrust start/stop cycles (asserted in tests).
- Tone.js is pinned and is the only new browser runtime dependency introduced.
- `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

# Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list

## Problem statement

When the mineral hold fills, the modal choice overlay lists each option as a bare name (for example `Spread Shot Lv.3`). The player cannot see **what an upgrade will actually change**, nor tell at a glance whether an offer is a **brand-new item** or an **upgrade to something they already own**. This makes the permanent-progression choice feel opaque.

## Users

- **Player (informed upgrade):** "As a player, when the hold fills and I'm offered an upgrade, I want to see exactly what improves — e.g. `+1 projectile, +36% bullet size` — so I can make an informed build choice."
- **Player (new vs upgrade):** "As a player, I want a brand-new item in the list clearly marked **New**, so I never confuse it with an upgrade to something I own."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the displayed summary derived from the shared level resolver, so the numbers shown can never drift from the numbers actually applied."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Upgrade summary.** Every hold-full choice option that upgrades a levelled item the player owns shows a change summary comparing its current level with the offered level (for example `+1 projectile, +36% bullet size`), listing **only the variables that actually change** (producer Q3 = A).
- **AC2 — New badge.** Every option for an item the player does **not** yet own is marked **New**.
- **AC3 — Single source of truth.** The summary is computed from the shared level maths (`resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`); no stat values or labels are duplicated in the scene or in a second copy (gym↔game parity convention).
- **AC4 — Detail line rendering.** `MineralChoiceScene` renders the summary / **New** badge as a **second, smaller detail line beneath the option name** (producer Q2 = B), leaving the existing option label (`"1.  Spread Shot Lv.3"`) unchanged.
- **AC5 — Generic mechanism.** The display mechanism is option-kind agnostic: any option that carries a level concept yields a summary. Power-up upgrade summaries activate automatically once AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 (power-up levels) supplies levels, with no change to the display code.
- **AC6 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`; no divergent copy is introduced.
- **AC7 — Testing/validation.** Unit and scene tests cover: delta computation (changed-only, formatting, no-change → no summary), **New** detection, overlay rendering of the detail line, and the no-summary fallback. Test coverage serves a meaningful purpose (TDD preferred).
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and Game Design Document §4.5.
- **AC9 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once (in `src/powerups/choice.ts` / `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` / `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`) and be consumed by both the game and every gym; gyms that open the choice are exercised by the same tests.
- **Backward compatibility:** extend `ChoiceOption` with **optional** fields so existing `ChoiceStrategy` implementations and tests keep compiling; the pluggable strategy contract is unchanged.
- **Keep the 3-offer mechanism unchanged** (producer-confirmed previously); this item changes presentation only.
- **Do not break existing option-label assertions:** `MineralChoiceScene.getOptionLabels()` is asserted in tests; the detail line is a separate game object, so labels stay intact.
- **No duplicated level maths:** reuse `weaponLevels.ts`; never re-derive caps/curves inline.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.
- **Scope boundary:** power-up **levels** are out of scope here and tracked by AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption { id, name, kind, level? }`; `buildChoiceCandidates(pool, context)` builds base-pool options plus one `weapon-level` offer per owned weapon (context = `{ weaponLevels }`); `toChoiceOption`; `randomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — modal overlay renders one centred `Text` per option at `210 + index * 64` with label `${index + 1}.  ${option.name}`; `getOptionLabels()`; keyboard `1..n` and pointer selection; single `onSelect(index, option)` contract.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `resolveWeaponAtLevel(weaponId, level)` returning `WeaponLevelStats`; `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` with per-variable `label`/`description`; MVP variables `fireRate`, `projectileCount`, `bulletSize`, `aoeRadius`, plus `planned` variables already specified.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getWeaponLevel(id)`, `getWeaponLevels()` → `[{ id, level }]`.
- Launchers — `PlayScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymWeaponLeveling.openMineralChoice` all pass `{ weaponLevels: player.getWeaponLevels() }` as the strategy context.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — `applyMineralChoiceReward` permanently equips (which increments the run-scoped level) for both `weapon` and `weapon-level` options.
- GDD §4.5 documents the choice overlay and the level-up offers.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the option model** — add optional display metadata to `ChoiceOption`, e.g. `isNew?: boolean` and `changeSummary?: string` (naming at implementation's discretion), keeping existing fields and strategies backward compatible.
2. **Populate the metadata in `buildChoiceCandidates`** (or a small pure helper it calls):
   - `weapon-level` offers (owned, levelled weapon): summary = formatted deltas between `resolveWeaponAtLevel(id, current)` and `resolveWeaponAtLevel(id, current + 1)`, listing only changed variables with readable formatting (counts as `+N <label>`, scalars as `+NN% <label>`).
   - base-pool **weapon** options: if the player does not own the weapon → `isNew = true`; if owned → the permanent-equip path increments the level, so treat it as an upgrade and show the same `current → current + 1` summary.
   - **power-up** options: if the player does not own it → `isNew = true`; upgrade summaries are deferred to AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6.
3. **Add a pure, unit-testable formatter** (e.g. `summariseWeaponLevelChange(weaponId, fromLevel, toLevel)` in `weaponLevels.ts`, or a new `src/powerups/choiceSummary.ts`) so the game and gyms share one implementation and no display strings live in scenes.
4. **Render the detail line** in `MineralChoiceScene` beneath each option name, in a smaller font/secondary colour; keep the primary label unchanged.
5. **Tests and documentation** as per AC7/AC8.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — extend `ChoiceOption`; populate `isNew` / `changeSummary` in `buildChoiceCandidates`.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` *(or new `src/powerups/choiceSummary.ts`)* — pure, shared change-summary formatter over `resolveWeaponAtLevel` + `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — render the second detail line; keep `getOptionLabels()` intact.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — supply ownership context (they already pass `weaponLevels`; extend only if power-up ownership context is needed).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — extend for summary/New.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts` *(or a new summary test)* — delta formatting.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 (and README feature pointer if present).

## Related work

- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed; parent of the level-curve system this displays).
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** — Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling (completed; built the `weapon-level` offers).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop minerals that fill the hold and grant a power-up choice (the overlay this extends).
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups *(new, `discovered-from:AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR`)* — enables power-up upgrade summaries via the generic mechanism.
- Game Design Document §4.5 (minerals, hold, hold-full choice).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (medium):** "all option kinds" could expand into designing power-up levels. Mitigation: this item ships the **generic display mechanism** plus weapon summaries; power-up levels are explicitly deferred to AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6.
- **Power-up "New" semantics (medium):** P3–P7 are transient and P9/P10 stack; "ownership" for the **New** badge may need extra context beyond `weaponLevels`. Assumption: mark power-ups as **New** when the player has never owned/collected them, using ownership context added to `ChoiceContext` (optional, backward compatible). If reliable ownership data is unavailable in MVP, power-up **New** may be limited to the base-pool definition; flagged as an implementation question.
- **Duplicate offers (low):** an owned weapon can appear both as a base-pool `weapon` option and a `weapon-level` option; both will show the same summary. Deduplicating is out of scope unless the producer requests it.
- **Test coupling (low):** existing `getOptionLabels()` assertions must keep passing — the detail line must not alter the primary label.
- **Formatter drift (low):** mitigation is a single pure formatter over `resolveWeaponAtLevel`, covered by tests and consumed identically by game and gyms.
- **Assumption (confirmed by non-objection):** "full hull" in the seed request means the **hold-full mineral choice** (the only player-facing selection list in the game).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded during intake for AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR (operator = Producer).

- **Q1 — Scope: which options get the treatment?** (A: every option — upgrades show a stat-change summary, unowned items show New; B: weapon options only; C: weapon-level upgrade offers only.)
  — **Answer (Producer):** **A**, and *"create a work item to design levels for all power-ups"*. Consequently AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 was created; this item builds the generic mechanism and covers weapon upgrades now.

- **Q2 — Presentation of the summary in the overlay?** (A: inline on the same row; B: a second, smaller detail line under the option name; C: a detail panel on hover/focus.)
  — **Answer (Producer):** **B** — a second, smaller detail line beneath the option name.

- **Q3 — What to show for the change summary?** (A: only the variables that change, human-readable; B: all MVP variables, even when unchanged; C: a short qualitative phrase.)
  — **Answer (Producer):** **A** — only changed variables, human-readable.

- **Assumption — "full hull":** interpreted as the **hold-full mineral choice** (the only selection list in the game). No objection raised.

## Summary

Power-ups (P3–P10) currently have **no level concept** — they are binary/timed or, for P9/P10, stack up to a capped count. This work item designs (and later implements) a per-power-up level curve so power-ups can be levelled up like weapons, enabling upgrade summaries and permanent progression in the hold-full choice.

Discovered from AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR ("Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list"), which must display a change summary for power-up upgrades once levels exist.

## User story
As a player, spending a hold-full mineral choice on a power-up I already own should measurably strengthen it, so power-ups scale across a run the way weapons do.

## Draft acceptance criteria (to be refined at intake/plan)
- AC1: A documented, data-driven level-curve design exists for every power-up in P3–P10 (comparable to `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`).
- AC2: Each power-up exposes a run-scoped integer level with monotonic, diminishing-returns effects and a finite cap.
- AC3: Existing stack semantics (P9/P10 cap 5) are reconciled with the new level model.
- AC4: A pure resolver maps `(powerUpId, level)` to effective stats, consumed by the same shared path in game and gyms.
- AC5: The hold-full choice can offer power-up level-ups and the summary/New display (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR) renders their deltas.
- AC6: Unit + parity tests cover the curve, resolver and integration.
- AC7: Documentation updated; full test suite passes.

## Context / reference
- Weapon levels: `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` (`WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`, `curveValue`, `resolveWeaponAtLevel`).
- Power-up catalogue: `src/powerups/types.ts` (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`, `maxStacks`, `duration`).
- Choice items: `src/powerups/choice.ts`; overlay: `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`.
